title: Codex Sol vs Astra
author: 907Renegade
selftext: Now that the Sol model has been out for a little bit, how have people experience been with switching between Sol and Astra? Im definitely noticing my usage lasts longer with Sol, but does anyone have anything good or bad to say about the quality of the code that Sol produces vs Astra?

comments.author: Mobile-Bedroom9175
comments.body: im using sol  . feels good so far

comments.author: count023
comments.body: i use sol medium for most of hte work and then tell it to dispatch astra agents as needed for deeper dives or reviews, seems to work well and doesnt burn all my usage up.

replies.author: 907Renegade
replies.body: Ive been using Sol high for any major things like damage calculations and anything thay may require some math/balancing and then Sol light for things like formatting/moving UI elements to make things look more organized or changing font sizes, etc. Seems to be working pretty well and my usage is definitely lasting much longer than on Astra light.

comments.author: Recoil42
comments.body: Sol simply doesn't handle 3D as well as Astra. It's Astra or bust for 3D.

replies.author: 907Renegade
replies.body: Thankfully im working on a 2d game. But ill keep that in mind if I ever decide to make a 3d game.

replies.author: Qottonmouth
replies.body: That is not my experience. Sol 6.1 Extra High has been testing controls in a 3D environment, even changing 1st person camera behaviour based on the orientation of your character

comments.author: Qottonmouth
comments.body: I tried Astra once, never again. It ate the weekly budget, did the job but added unnecessary extras for some reason. Sol 6.1 Extra High can do the most advanced tasks with nearly no usage from my experience

comments.author: Creepy-Doughnut-5054
comments.body: I use Astra SOLELY for asset production in various tools like blender or audacity, models, details, animations and so on. On everything else it's just overkill and Sol is absolutely enough for these.

comments.author: Upper-Philosophy2376
comments.body: I've gone back to the old pattern of having the smarter model make a plan and the other model do that plan. It's working fine.

replies.author: 907Renegade
replies.body: That's kinda what I've been doing with switching to Sol High for planning and calculations and stuff and then switching back to low for the implementations and easy stuff.

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
Sol is extremely competent. 

Astra is a fckn genius. 

  
The difference in usage, though, is staggering. Astra will eat through your weekly allotment in a day, easy. Sol... I've never hit the limit on it.

Astra's only usable for me right now because of the reasonably generous weekly resets. But that will no doubt change. 

  
The meat and potatoes of a project likely needs to be done by Sol for cost's sake. But if there's a complex job and you hardly know where to begin, ask Astra. There is nothing it cannot do (that's a lie, but you know what I mean).

comments.author: Trojanheadcoach
comments.body:
Sol is cool and way better than where we were at a few months ago but it’ll overlook simple stuff sometimes. I don’t see any performance difference in the sol modes honestly. Higher thinking seems to just take a bit longer to make the same mistakes. 

Anything nuanced or complex I’m using astra, but I use a ton of astra low and only increase if it’s a huge task. Astra is expensive and not perfect but it’s definitely a different tier than sol and made me rethink how good ts can actually become.

comments.author: tamal4444
comments.body: I use Sol high and it is sufficient for me. I hope local models catch up to Sol 6.1 high.
